problemStatement.plain: AVAILABLE: **Does an analogous result hold for hypergraphs: must non-Ramsey r-uniform hype.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE (axiomatized): verified r-uniform hypergraph framework for oq-03 — complement symmetry (all r), 2^n ceiling, and edge-count hardness lemma proved with 0 sorries; open exponential lower bound isolated as the single axiom shelah_hypergraph.
builtItems: homogeneous_compl / nonRamsey_compl: complement symmetry for all r (Erdos1036HypergraphOQ03.lean:133,156)
distinct_edgeCounts_le: polynomial ceiling on the edge-count invariant (Erdos1036HypergraphOQ03.lean:177)
insights: Complement symmetry of non-Ramseyness generalizes to ALL uniformities r: for e ⊆ S with |e|=r, e∈Hᶜ ↔ e∉H, so the all-edges/no-edges homogeneity disjuncts swap (homogeneous_compl, nonRamsey_compl).

The edge-count invariant of induced sub-hypergraphs takes only ≤ |E(H)|+1 (polynomially many) values, so no single numeric isomorphism-invariant can certify 2^{Ω(n)} distinct classes — pinpoints why the lower bound is hard (distinct_edgeCounts_le).
As in base #1036, the tractable diversity count is the LABELLED induced-edge-set count (upper proxy for isomorphism-class count); a genuine iso-class count needs a quotient construction.
mathlibGaps: No isomorphism-class quotient for finite hypergraphs (needed to replace the labelled-count proxy with the true non-isomorphic count).
No r-uniform analogue of Shelah 1998 / Hales-Jewett partition argument in Mathlib — the exponential lower bound remains an open axiom.
nextSteps: Replace numDistinctInduced (labelled) with a genuine isomorphism-class count via a quotient by hypergraph iso.
Attempt a verified 2^{Ω(n)} lower-bound WITNESS for an explicit non-Ramsey r-uniform family (r=3), demonstrating the phenomenon is realizable even if the general bound stays open.
Investigate whether an r-uniform Hales-Jewett argument can discharge shelah_hypergraph.
